labels.label: prop:ring_both_continuous_extends
labels.notes:
Unmarked and partial. That is correct: the T_A half is false as printed, and the f_A half rests on the OQ-42 (c) reading of f. The proposition's A_2 also depends on the l.52 claim, which is false for Z/2Z. Every hypothesis the closer adds is in the checklist and SCOPE: IsZ2Ring including integrality (OQ-42 (a), load-bearing, with the places it is used), 2 ≠ 0 wherever A_2 or ι enters (OQ-42 (b)), 3x+1 ≠ 0 for T (OQ-42 (d)), and the readings of the topology and of A_2. None is hidden.

THE ASSEMBLIES. ring_both_continuous_extends (Completion.lean:977) takes [CommRing A] [IsZ2Ring A] [UniformSpace A] [IsUniformAddGroup A] [IsTopologicalRing A], hA : IsAdic (span {2}) and h2 : 2 ≠ 0. It concludes:
(i) f continuous on A.
(ii) T ContinuousOn {3x+1 ≠ 0}. This set contains every point of 2A+1 where the paper's T_A exists, so (ii) is at least the printed 'T_A continuous'.
(iii) f on UniformSpace.Completion A is continuous, satisfies f(↑x) = ↑(f x), and is the only continuous g with that property.
(iv) T on the completion is ContinuousOn {3w+1 ≠ 0}, satisfies T(↑x) = ↑(T x), and is the only g continuous on {Odd ∧ 3w+1 ≠ 0} that agrees with T_A on the odd x with 3x+1 ≠ 0.
(v) There is an odd w₀ with 3w₀+1 = 0 at which no such g is continuous within 2A_2+1.
ring_both_continuous_extends_padicInt (:1004) is the same statement in ℤ₂ through ι, with h2 its only extra hypothesis. Both are at least the corrected forms the REPORT claims.

NON-VACUITY. A /tmp probe, since deleted, instantiated ring_both_continuous_extends at A = ℤ_[2] (isAdic_padicInt) and at an arbitrary IsZ2Ring A with the canonical WithIdeal ⟨span {2}⟩ structure. Both elaborate. instIsZ2RingZMod2 exists, so Findings 3 and 4 concern rings that satisfy the paper's definition.

FINDING 1 (T does not extend), checked. T_int_not_extends states ¬∃ g : ℤ₂ → ℤ₂, ContinuousOn g {Odd} ∧ ∀ x : ℤ, Odd x → g x = T x. In ℤ, 3x+1 ≠ 0 for every x, so T_ℤ is the paper's map on all of 2ℤ+1. ContinuousOn on 2ℤ₂+1 is the weakest reading of « extends continuously to A_2 »: a map continuous on all of A_2 is in particular continuous on 2A_2+1. The refutation therefore covers both readings and is not a strawman. not_exists_continuousWithinAt_extension_T is stronger still: for every A with 2 ≠ 0 it asks only continuity within 2ℤ₂+1 at the single point −1/3, and agreement only where T_A is the paper's map. The completion form (:948) is the same statement in UniformSpace.Completion A.
I checked the −1/3 argument by hand. For c_j = (4^{j+1}−1)/3 = 1+4+…+4^j (odd), 3c_j+1 = 2^{2j+2}, so T(c_j) = 1. For d_j = 10c_j+3 (odd), 3d_j+1 = 5·2^{2j+3}, so T(d_j) = 5. Both sequences lie in 2A+1, and both tend to −1/3 because c + 1/3 = (3c+1)/3 with 3 a unit. In the Lean, hconv divides out 3 with two_pow_dvd_of_dvd_three_pow_mul. A function continuous within 2A_2+1 at −1/3 would take both values 1 and 5 there, and 1 ≠ 5 because 4 ≠ 0. The argument is correct.
printed_T_extends_false is mathematically right: its witness is B = ℤ. Its statement is formally a little weaker than 'the printed statement is refuted' (minor finding 1).

FINDING 2 (T is continuous where defined), checked. continuousAt_T / continuousOn_T hold for 3x+1 ≠ 0, Z/2Z included. continuous_T_of_not_isUnit_three gives continuity on all of A when 3 ∉ Aˣ.

l.52, A_2 ≃ ℤ₂. completion_ringEquiv takes A₂ = Mathlib's UniformSpace.Completion A for any uniform structure making A a uniform additive group and a topological ring whose topology is IsAdic (span {2}). That uniformity is not a convenient choice. For a uniform add group, uniformity_eq_comap_nhds_zero makes the uniformity a function of the topology (checked in the probe), so its entourages are {(x,y) | 2ⁿ ∣ y − x}. This is the uniformity of |x| = 2^{-ν₂(x)}, whose balls are x + 2ⁿA (hasBasis_nhds_two). The conclusion is a RingEquiv Completion A ≃+* ℤ₂ with e ↑x = ι x, uniformly continuous in both directions. It is built from AbstractCompletion.compareEquiv on the package (ℤ₂, ι): injective by Krull, dense image, inducing. completion_twoAdic shows the hypotheses hold for the canonical WithIdeal structure.
Reading 'the 2-completion' as this uniform completion is fair. For any ring and ideal I, the Hausdorff completion for the I-adic uniformity is canonically lim A/IⁿA; this is standard (Atiyah–Macdonald ch. 10). Mathlib at the pin has no AdicCompletion ≃ UniformSpace.Completion bridge (grep of RingTheory/AdicCompletion and Topology finds none). The file proves the compatible isomorphisms ℤ/2ⁿℤ ≃ A/2ⁿA (zmodEquivQuotient, zmodPow_compat), and ℤ₂ is their limit (PadicInt.lift). So the algebraic lim A/2ⁿA ≅ ℤ₂ is one step away. As the REPORT says, it is not formalized as an AdicCompletion statement. 'Naturally' is covered by toZ2_unique, toZ2_comp and ringEquiv_padicInt_unique (any two ring isos B ≃ ℤ₂ are equal).

FINDING 3 (Z/2Z), checked. completion_zmod2_not_padicInt universally quantifies the instance binders [UniformSpace (ZMod 2)] [IsUniformAddGroup (ZMod 2)] [IsTopologicalRing (ZMod 2)]. These are exactly what UniformSpace.Completion needs to be a ring, so 'for any uniform ring structure' is what is proved. It does not even require the topology to be 2-adic. The conclusion is IsEmpty (Completion (ZMod 2) ≃+* ℤ_[2]): no ring isomorphism at all, because 2 = 0 passes through coeRingHom. ZMod 2 is an IsZ2Ring (instIsZ2RingZMod2), so the finding about l.52 as printed is true. Whether Z/2Z is meant to be excluded is OQ-42 (b).

zmod4_witness is genuine. ZMod 4 is noetherian, ZMod 4/(2) ≃ ZMod 2 (quotient_two_of_parity, by decide), 2 ≠ 0, and ¬IsDomain since 2·2 = 0. For every uniform ring structure, its completion has 4 = 0, so no ring iso to ℤ₂ exists. ZMod 4 satisfies l.52's definition (noetherian, A/2A ≅ Z/2Z) and l.50's claim 2 ≠ 0, and fails only integrality. This supports 'integrality is load-bearing for l.52' (OQ-42 (a)).

THE f HALF is the printed claim under OQ-42 (c) and 2 ≠ 0. f_{A_2} is the paper's map there because isZ2Ring_completion and two_ne_zero_completion hold.

TRUTH. I re-read every SCOPE bullet and checklist row against the Lean. All are true, with two qualifications. First, the claim that printed_T_extends_false refutes 'the printed statement' (:68, :645–646) is formally slightly too strong; see minor finding 1. Second, the A₂ row says '✓ carried' although it is a reading (the SCOPE bullet at :92–96 and REPORT question 2 disclose it). The uniform completion for the I-adic uniformity is canonically lim A/IⁿA, so the row is defensible and no finding is raised. findings.where: Completion.lean:647–650 (printed_T_extends_false), with its docstring :645–646, SCOPE :67–68, and REPORT labels[0].findings[0] ('The printed statement, quantified over all Z/2Z-rings with 2 ≠ 0, is refuted')
findings.what: The agreement clause of the negated universal is `∀ x : B, Odd x → g (toZ2 h2 x) = toZ2 h2 (T x)`. It has no `3 * x + 1 ≠ 0`, so for rings B containing −1/3 (ℤ_[2], ℤ_(2)) the body also demands g(ι(−1/3)) = ι(T(−1/3)) = 0. That is Lean's junk value; the paper imposes no such condition, because T_B is undefined there. The universal that is refuted is therefore stronger than the printed one, and its negation is formally weaker than 'the printed statement is false'. The mathematics is unaffected. The proof's witness is B = ℤ, which has no junk point. T_int_not_extends is the faithful refutation at ℤ. not_exists_continuousWithinAt_extension_T refutes the faithful form, agreement only where 3x+1 ≠ 0, for every A with 2 ≠ 0. A probe confirmed that the faithful variant of printed_T_extends_false is proved by the same three lines, passing hgT directly.
findings.fix: Add `3 * x + 1 ≠ 0 →` to the agreement clause of printed_T_extends_false (proof: `exact not_exists_continuousWithinAt_extension_T (A := ℤ) two_ne_zero ⟨g, hg _ odd_inv3.neg, hgT⟩`). Otherwise reword its docstring and the REPORT finding to cite T_int_not_extends / not_exists_continuousWithinAt_extension_T as the refutation of the printed statement.

notes: There is no major finding. The single label is correctly unmarked and partial. Every added hypothesis (integrality via IsZ2Ring, 2 ≠ 0, 3x+1 ≠ 0) and every reading (the IsAdic topology, A₂ as UniformSpace.Completion, f halving the even) is disclosed in the checklist, SCOPE and REPORT. The assemblies are at least the corrected forms claimed, and they are non-vacuous. All four paper findings are true. (1) T_A has no continuous extension at −1/3, even under the weakest reading of 'extends continuously'; the c_j/d_j argument is correct. (2) T_A is continuous wherever it is defined. (3) l.52 fails for Z/2Z under any uniform ring structure. (4) ZMod 4 shows that integrality is needed for l.52. The uniform structure on A is forced to be the 2-adic one by IsUniformAddGroup + IsAdic, the completion is Mathlib's UniformSpace.Completion, and the reading agrees with lim A/2ⁿA by a standard fact that is not in Mathlib at the pin. Completion.lean can graduate with or without the minor fix; the fix only tightens how one declaration's statement corresponds to the paper.
